1.title: Amid brutal sell-off, what comes next for Google, Amazon and other Big Tech titans?
1.summary: Soaring artificial intelligence revenues have failed to shield Intel, Amazon and Google’s parent company Alphabet from a brutal Wall Street sell-off, as their latest quarterly results deepened investor jitters over mounting capital spending and delayed returns. Intel plunged about 23 per cent in extended trading on Thursday, while Amazon shed 7.3 per cent. 1.title: Amazon, Intel shares crash up to 25% in premarket trade as AI spending concerns trigger tech sell-off - What's next?
1.summary: Amazon shares fell 7.4% and Intel plunged 25% in premarket trading as investors reacted to weak business outlooks and rising AI investment costs. The sell-off weighed on other chipmakers and reflected growing concern that heavy spending is eroding Big Tech cash flows.

33.title: Japan to Tap $7 Billion from Government Fund to Subsidize Gasoline Prices
33.summary: Japan’s government on Friday decided to tap $7 billion from its contingency reserves to keep subsidies for gasoline and other fuels, even as it plans to gradually scale back the support from December. The Japanese government decided today to allocate about $7 billion (1.1 trillion Japanese yen) from the reserve funds to continue capping retail gasoline prices amid soaring oil and fuel import costs, Japanese media reported. 3.title: Binance pledges to cover losses after US$6 billion crypto hack
3.summary: Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume, has pledged to cover all losses from a hack that it said drained around US$6.3 billion from its wallet. At that scale, it would be the biggest crypto theft on record, surpassing the US$1.5 billion stolen from Dubai-based exchange Bybit in February 2025, a theft the FBI attributed to North Korea. Binance said in a post on X on Friday that it had suspended all deposits and withdrawals while its team conducts security checks,..

37.title: Bank of Japan says inflation hit 2% target after 13 years
37.summary: The Bank of Japan said on Friday inflation had hit its 2% target, more than 13 years after it adopted the goal in a bid to pull the economy out of deflation, but held off hiking interest rates for now.

37.title: Bank of Japan declares victory in hitting price target, signals near-term hikes
